title: Staged rollout plan + backout procedure for marketplace onboarding changes
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Create a staged rollout plan for the marketplace purchase → entitlement → org-linking onboarding changes (AWS + GCP). Plan must include: feature flag strategy, canary phases, monitoring/alerts, comms + approvals, and a concrete backout procedure that Support/SRE can execute during launch.

Context
We’re shipping multiple coordinated changes:
- Entitlement ingestion + mapping (AWS/GCP SKU IDs → internal entitlements)
- Webhook validation + audit logging for provisioning events
- Console onboarding wizard + org-linking UX + entitlement status display
- Billing plan code updates (minimal changes to support new SKUs)
- Docs/quickstarts for marketplace buyers

Because these changes affect activation and revenue capture, rollout must be reversible without requiring a full deploy rollback, and must keep idempotency guarantees intact (no duplicated entitlements, no double-grants).

Rollout principles
1) Safe-by-default: new behavior is gated; default path continues to be “legacy marketplace onboarding flow.”
2) No silent partial activation: if any step is disabled (e.g., org linking), Console must clearly show entitlement state + next action.
3) Idempotent + replayable: backout must not lose events; ability to reprocess queued/failed events is required.
4) Observable: every phase has explicit go/no-go metrics and alert coverage.

Proposed feature flags (LaunchDarkly)
- mp_onboarding_v2_enabled (global): Master gate for all v2 behavior. Default OFF.
- mp_onboarding_v2_console_wizard (console): Enables Console wizard + new UI states.
- mp_onboarding_v2_entitlement_mapping (control plane): Enables new SKU mapping layer in production.
- mp_onboarding_v2_webhook_ingestion (control plane): Enables accepting/processing provisioning webhooks via the new pipeline.
- mp_onboarding_v2_gcp_path (control plane): Enables GCP-specific ingestion/mapping path.
- mp_onboarding_v2_auto_org_link (control plane): Enables auto-link suggestion/flow based on purchaser identifiers (kept OFF until proven safe).

Targeting rules
- Target by environment: dev/staging/prod.
- In prod, target by:
  - Cloud: aws | gcp
  - Region: start with us-west-2 (AWS) and us-central1 (GCP) if supported by partner review constraints
  - Allowlist: Redwood-internal test accounts + named pilot customers (Sales/Partnerships confirmed)
  - Percentage rollout (only after allowlist is stable)

Rollout phases
Phase 0 — Pre-flight (staging only)
- Flags:
  - Enable all v2 flags in staging.
- Entry criteria:
  - ENG-4410 integration tests passing in CI for AWS + GCP fixtures.
  - Staging synthetic purchases validated end-to-end (purchase event → entitlement granted → Console shows status → org linked).
- Exit criteria:
  - 0 critical bugs in Console wizard flows.
  - Webhook processing idempotency validated (replay same event N times → single entitlement grant).

Phase 1 — Prod dark launch (no user-facing change)
- Flags:
  - mp_onboarding_v2_enabled: OFF
  - mp_onboarding_v2_webhook_ingestion: ON (shadow mode)
  - mp_onboarding_v2_entitlement_mapping: ON (shadow evaluation only; no grants)
- Implementation detail:
  - Shadow mode means we ingest + validate + log, but do not write entitlements. We emit “decision logs” that compare legacy mapping vs v2 mapping, stored in audit logs/metrics.
- Entry criteria:
  - Monitoring dashboards live (ENG-4407) and on-call runbook drafted.
- Exit criteria:
  - Mapping parity >= 99.5% across observed events for 72 hours.
  - No increase in webhook failure rate.

Phase 2 — Allowlist canary (internal + 1–2 pilot customers)
- Flags:
  - mp_onboarding_v2_enabled: ON (allowlist only)
  - mp_onboarding_v2_webhook_ingestion: ON
  - mp_onboarding_v2_entitlement_mapping: ON
  - mp_onboarding_v2_console_wizard: ON (allowlist only)
  - mp_onboarding_v2_auto_org_link: OFF
- Scope:
  - AWS first (GCP held behind mp_onboarding_v2_gcp_path until AWS stabilizes)
- Entry criteria:
  - Support macros + escalation path published (ENG-4409).
  - Partner review feedback accounted for (no copy/security claim blockers to shipping behavior).
- Exit criteria (24–48h minimum):
  - Entitlement lag p95 <= 5 minutes.
  - Webhook validation failure rate < 0.5%.
  - Provisioning error rate < 1%.
  - 0 cases of “wrong org linked” for allowlist cohort.

Phase 3 — Percentage canary (AWS 5% → 25% → 50%)
- Flags:
  - mp_onboarding_v2_enabled: ON for AWS purchasers by percentage
  - mp_onboarding_v2_console_wizard: ON for same cohort
- Ramp schedule:
  - 5% for 24h → 25% for 24h → 50% for 48h.
  - Hold at each step if any alert triggers (see Monitoring & alerts).
- Exit criteria:
  - No sustained regressions vs baseline week:
    - Activation success rate (purchase → usable org entitlement) not down > 1.0% absolute.
    - Support ticket rate for marketplace onboarding not up > 25% relative.

Phase 4 — Full rollout (AWS 100%, then GCP)
- AWS: move to 100% once Phase 3 criteria met.
- GCP: repeat Phase 2–4 using mp_onboarding_v2_gcp_path gate. Start with allowlist + region targeting to reduce validation blast radius.

Monitoring & alerts (must be live before Phase 2)
Dashboards (owner: Allison Grant / Rafael Mendes)
- Marketplace onboarding funnel
  - purchase_event_received_count
  - entitlement_grant_success_count
  - org_link_completed_count
  - activation_success_rate = org_link_completed / purchase_event_received
- Lag metrics
  - entitlement_lag_seconds (p50/p95/p99)
- Failures
  - webhook_validation_failure_count (by reason)
  - webhook_processing_failure_count (by step)
  - mapping_no_match_count (SKU not mapped)
- Console UX
  - wizard_error_state_rate
  - “contact support” click-through rate for marketplace screens

Alerts (page thresholds; adjust after 1 week baseline)
- P1 page: entitlement_lag p95 > 15 minutes for 15 min (prod)
- P1 page: webhook_processing_failure_rate > 2% for 10 min
- P2 page: mapping_no_match_count > 5 in 30 min (new SKUs missing mapping)
- P2 page: activation_success_rate drops > 2% absolute over 30 min window

Backout procedure (operator playbook)
Primary goal: stop new grants/links quickly while preserving event data for replay.

Backout Level 1 — Disable customer-facing wizard only (UI backout)
Use when: Console wizard UX is confusing/buggy but backend entitlements are fine.
- Action:
  - Set mp_onboarding_v2_console_wizard = OFF (or narrow targeting to internal only).
- Expected behavior:
  - Existing marketplace entitlements still grant; Console shows legacy instructions + entitlement status page.
- Verification:
  - Console error state rate returns to baseline within 15 minutes.

Backout Level 2 — Stop v2 entitlement grants (control plane backout)
Use when: mapping errors, wrong entitlements, or billing/metering mismatch suspected.
- Action (in order):
  1) Set mp_onboarding_v2_enabled = OFF (global)
  2) Set mp_onboarding_v2_entitlement_mapping = OFF (or to shadow mode)
  3) Keep mp_onboarding_v2_webhook_ingestion = ON in “record-only” mode if supported; otherwise disable processing but retain raw payload storage.
- Expected behavior:
  - New purchases follow legacy grant path (if legacy still enabled) OR go into “pending activation” state with clear support instructions (no silent drop).
- Data integrity notes:
  - Ensure we do not delete any “v2 attempted” grant records; keep for reconciliation.

Backout Level 3 — Pause all marketplace provisioning processing (hard stop)
Use when: security concern, webhook signature validation bug, or severe data integrity issue.
- Action:
  - Disable mp_onboarding_v2_webhook_ingestion (and/or set worker concurrency to 0 via config) to stop processing.
  - Confirm raw webhook payloads continue to be accepted/stored OR that the marketplace provider will retry (document provider behavior).
- Customer handling:
  - Support posts status + provides manual activation path where possible (internal runbook + templated email).
- Recovery:
  - Re-enable ingestion after fix, then run replay/backfill job for paused interval.

Reconciliation / replay steps (after any Level 2/3 backout)
- Identify affected purchases:
  - Query by time window + cohort targeting rules.
  - Export list of marketplace entitlement events and their processing status.
- Reprocess:
  - Run idempotent replay job (from ENG-4401/ENG-4402 codepath) for failed/paused events.
- Validate:
  - Compare counts: purchase events vs entitlement grants vs org links.
  - Spot-check 5–10 accounts for correct org + entitlement set.

Approvals / comms
- Go/No-Go meeting required before Phase 2:
  - Connor O’Brien (release), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Ethan Park (control plane), Chloe Martin (console), Dev Patel (support), Soojin Lee (PMM), Marcus Lin (security).
- Change announcement:
  - Post in #eng, #support, #partnerships when moving between phases.
  - Document current flag targeting + phase in the on-call runbook.

Acceptance criteria
- Written rollout plan stored in internal runbook (linked from this ticket) with:
  - Flag names + targeting rules
  - Phase checklist + explicit entry/exit criteria
  - Alert thresholds + dashboard links
  - Backout levels 1–3 with step-by-step operator instructions
  - Reconciliation/replay guidance
- Dry-run executed in staging and at least one prod internal allowlist account.
- Support lead signs off that backout steps align with customer comms macros and escalation routing.

Open questions
- Do we need provider-side listing changes coordinated with rollout phases (e.g., new fulfillment URLs)? If yes, add explicit dependency on Partnerships submission timing.
- Confirm “record-only” webhook behavior: can we accept + store raw payloads even when processing is paused? If not, document provider retry semantics for AWS vs GCP.
